relevance.rationale: Companion to 1402.4615 and the more general of the two: it introduces a large class of random Young diagrams built from an arbitrary character family (chi_lambda) via P^chi (§1.4 eq. (1.1)), specialises it to Jack characters, and proves limit shape plus asymptotically Gaussian fluctuations for the whole class. The folio's conj:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton part (3) is an open weak-convergence statement for a measure of exactly that P^chi form (the q-deformed Wedderburn weight dim_q^2/[n]_q!), and its part (2) already cites feray2010 from the same school. So the framework is the right shape; the deformation is not the same one, and no hypothesis has been checked for the q-weight. Technique/context, not a discharge. Corpus-grep: no ref() entry, no Śniady/Dołęga hit.

keyResults.statement: For a family (chi_lambda) of characters on partitions one defines a measure P^chi on Young diagrams; taking chi = Jack characters chi^(alpha)_lambda (alpha=1 recovers symmetric-group characters) yields a one-parameter class containing the classical ensembles.
keyResults.useForFolio: The general P^chi construction is the abstract slot the folio's mu_n^(q) = (iota_n)_* w~_lambda occupies. Cite as the framework in which a q-analogue of part (3) would be stated, naming the character family as the input that must be supplied.

keyResults.statement: Each such Jack-deformed random Young diagram converges to a limit shape, and fluctuations around the limit are asymptotically Gaussian.
keyResults.useForFolio: The template statement for the folio's open 'q-deformed Kerov-Vershik convergence'. Records that the deformed statement is a theorem for one deformation, so part (3) is plausibly reachable rather than speculative — while remaining silent on the q case.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan; needed to cite the P^chi framework at the open part (3).

Same discipline as its companion 1402.4615: the Jack alpha-deformation is not the folio's q-deformation and hypotheses are unchecked, so this is a remark recording the precedent and the required input, not aid-proof. One remark can cover both Jack papers.
